Each face of a triangular prism is coloured with a colour in such a way that no two adjacent faces have the same colour. What is the MINIMUM number of colours required to do this?
Note: Two faces are said to be adjacent if they share a common edge
a) 2
b) 3
c) 4
d) 5
My answer
Dyna Thinking Coach
Bridge
connect to everyday life
Picture a tent or a Toblerone box: 2 triangle ends and 3 rectangle sides. Faces that share an edge need different colours.
Slicer
break it into small parts
Colour in parts. First the 3 rectangles: does each one touch the other two? Then the front triangle: which faces does it touch? Then the back triangle.
YOUR TURN
Can the two triangles share a colour? Count the colours you used in all.
